source: src/live.md (old Notion page 'GPU architecture: Ampere to Blackwell', fetched 2026-09-22, copied from the parent's src/read/old/01_gpu_architecture.md)

items.fact: Best resources: Modal GPU Glossary, scaling book GPUs, H100 whitepaper, Blackwell architecture page, Chips and Cheese, Horace He
items.verdict: verified; carried (H100 whitepaper and Blackwell page replaced by NVIDIA's in-depth blogs for Ampere, Hopper, Blackwell Ultra and Rubin, which this page cites)

items.fact: GPU is a grid of SMs: 108 A100, 132 H100, 170 RTX 5090
items.verdict: verified (A100/Hopper blogs, RTX Blackwell whitepaper)

items.fact: 148 SMs per die on B200
items.verdict: corrected: 148 SMs per GPU (two dies), from an independent paper and the scaling book; NVIDIA's fetched pages do not state it; Blackwell Ultra is 160 SMs in 8 GPCs

items.fact: 4 processing blocks per SM, each with a warp scheduler
items.verdict: verified (scaling book; Hopper blog)

items.fact: warp = 32 threads in lockstep, SIMT; scheduler issues one ready warp's instruction per cycle
items.verdict: verified

items.fact: latency hidden by oversubscription; up to 64 resident warps per SM
items.verdict: verified (CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2); per generation 64 or 48

items.fact: ~400 cycles on a DRAM load
items.verdict: corrected: 466 (A100), 479 (H800), 542 (RTX 4090) cycles, Luo et al. Table IV

items.fact: occupancy and coalesced memory access matter
items.verdict: verified; occupancy limits per CC and the counter-case (low-occupancy tensor kernels) added; coalescing linked to the CUDA topic

items.fact: branch divergence inside a warp halves throughput
items.verdict: corrected and measured: cost is the sum of paths taken (1.95x for 2, 38.6x for 32 on the M1 GPU); divergence across warps is free

items.fact: per SM: 4 tensor cores, 256 KB register file, up to 228 KB shared memory/L1 on Hopper; 50 MB L2 on H100
items.verdict: verified; L1/shared is 256 KB of which up to 228 KB shared

items.fact: tensor cores are small MMA units; each generation widens the op and adds cheaper formats
items.verdict: verified and extended (per-SM rates, instruction families)

items.fact: Ampere 3rd gen: TF32, BF16, 2:4 sparsity; mma.sync; cp.async
items.verdict: verified (A100 blog; PTX ISA)

items.fact: Hopper 4th gen: FP8 E4M3/E5M2 + Transformer Engine; TMA, wgmma, clusters + DSMEM
items.verdict: verified; Transformer Engine not discussed (software library)

items.fact: Ada (4090): 4th gen, FP8, no TMA/wgmma, Ampere-style mma
items.verdict: verified 4th gen and FP8 (RTX whitepaper Appendix A); no wgmma consistent with sm_89; TMA absence not separately checked, not repeated

items.fact: Blackwell DC 5th gen: FP4/FP6, MXFP4, NVFP4; tcgen05.mma; TMEM 256 KB per SM; 2nd-gen Transformer Engine
items.verdict: verified (Blackwell Ultra blog; PTX ISA)

items.fact: Blackwell GeForce (5090, sm_120): FP4, FP8; TMA available but no TMEM/tcgen05; kernels look Ada-like
items.verdict: verified by real compiles on the CUDA topic (TMA and clusters compile for sm_120; wgmma and tcgen05 do not)

items.fact: TMA: per-SM DMA engine, multidimensional tiles from a descriptor, one thread issues, enables warp-specialised pipelines
items.verdict: verified (Hopper blog: 1D-5D; FlashAttention-3 abstract for warp specialisation)

items.fact: wgmma: asynchronous, warpgroup of 4 warps (128 threads), operands from shared memory; peak only via wgmma
items.verdict: verified and quantified: mma reaches 62.9% of Hopper's peak, wgmma 96.4% (Luo et al.)

items.fact: thread block clusters: co-scheduled blocks on adjacent SMs read each other's shared memory (DSMEM), a new locality tier
items.verdict: verified (Hopper blog: within a GPC, up to 16 blocks, about 7x faster than global; Luo: 180 cycles, 3.27 TB/s)

items.fact: tcgen05 accumulates into TMEM instead of registers, freeing registers for the epilogue
items.verdict: verified; shown in the tile animation

items.fact: a single MMA can span 2 SMs
items.verdict: verified (Blackwell Ultra blog 'dual-thread-block MMA'; PTX cta_group::2)

items.fact: NVFP4: FP8 scale per 16 values; doubles throughput over FP8; inference on Blackwell/Rubin standardising on it
items.verdict: scale format owned by the parent page s4 (linked); doubling verified for B200 (9,000 vs 4,500) but B300 is 3x and Rubin 2x FP8; 'standardising' dropped as unsourced

items.fact: HBM: stacked DRAM on interposer, 1024-bit per stack, slow-clocked; H100 3.35, H200 4.8, B200 8 TB/s, Rubin HBM4 ~13 TB/s
items.verdict: technology owned by the Memory technology sibling; bandwidths verified except Rubin, corrected to 22 TB/s (HGX page, Rubin blog; NVL72 page says 19.2)

items.fact: GDDR: discrete chips, narrower bus; 5090 GDDR7 512-bit, 1.79 TB/s, 32 GB, no ECC by default
items.verdict: verified except ECC (unconfirmed, dropped); technology details owned by Memory technology

items.fact: bandwidth is the number to memorise; decode and pointwise ops are bandwidth bound
items.verdict: carried via ridge points; depth on parent and Performance math

items.fact: ridge ~295 for H100 BF16 and rising every generation
items.verdict: corrected: BF16 ridge 153 A100, 295 H100, 281 B200, 182 Rubin; rises only at FP8 (591, 563, 795)

items.fact: NVLink per GPU: A100 600, H100 900 GB/s, B200/B300 1.8 TB/s; NVSwitch all-to-all; 8 in HGX, 72 in NVL72 (130 TB/s)
items.verdict: owned by the Interconnects sibling; H100 900 GB/s and 5090 PCIe used here

items.fact: GeForce since 4090 has no NVLink; dual 5090s talk over PCIe 5.0 x16 ~64 GB/s per direction, ~28x less than H100 NVLink
items.verdict: corrected: 7x per direction (64 vs 450), 14x against the 900 GB/s total; the dual-5090 framing dropped (no NVIDIA GPU here)

items.fact: across a 5090 pair prefer DP or PP over TP
items.verdict: owned by Interconnects and Distributed Training; dropped here

items.fact: 5090 vs H100 table: SMs/CUDA cores 170/21,760 vs 132/16,896
items.verdict: verified (128 lanes per SM)

items.fact: BF16 ~210 (FP32 acc, half rate) vs 989; FP8 ~419 vs 1,979
items.verdict: verified (209.5, 419 FP32 accumulate)

items.fact: FP4 dense ~838 on 5090
items.verdict: corrected: 1,676 dense (whitepaper Appendix A)

items.fact: 32 GB GDDR7 vs 80 GB HBM3; 1.79 vs 3.35 TB/s; PCIe 5.0 vs NVLink 4 900 GB/s; 575 vs 700 W
items.verdict: verified

items.fact: reading: 5090 about half an H100 for bandwidth-bound inference that fits; far behind for training (half-rate accumulate, no NVLink, 32 GB); kernel-dev target for sm_120
items.verdict: verified and carried

items.fact: datacenter table A100 2020 80 GB HBM2e 2.0 TB/s 312 BF16 400 W
items.verdict: verified (2,039 GB/s)
verified

items.fact: H200 2024 141 GB HBM3e 4.8 TB/s same compute 700 W
items.verdict: verified; announced Nov 13 2023 (year corrected to 2023 for the announcement)
capacity corrected (180 GB HGX/DGX per GPU); power corrected (up to 1,200 W, NVIDIA blog Table 2; 1,000 W unconfirmed); peaks verified (HGX)

items.fact: B300 2025 288 GB 8 TB/s FP4 dense 15 PF 1,400 W
items.verdict: verified (blog: 15 PF per GPU; HGX B300 gives 13.5 per GPU from board totals; atlas and s10 use HGX)

items.fact: Rubin H2 2026 288 GB HBM4 ~13 TB/s ~50 PF NVFP4 inference, power 'higher'
items.verdict: corrected: 22 TB/s; 50 PF is sparse inference, 35 PF dense training; power not stated

items.fact: MI400 (AMD) 432 GB HBM4 ~24 TB/s 2.9 EF per Helios rack
items.verdict: owned by the TPUs and other accelerators sibling and the parent's Chip atlas (23.3 TB/s, FP4)

items.fact: B200 two reticle-limit dies, 10 TB/s NV-HBI, one GPU; first mainstream chiplet NVIDIA GPU
items.verdict: verified except 'first' (dropped)

items.fact: Blackwell Ultra trades FP64/INT for 50% more FP4 and 288 GB
items.verdict: verified (FP64 1.25 TF, INT8 187.5 TOPS per GPU from HGX B300; 15 vs 10 PF)

items.fact: Vera Rubin (Vera CPU + Rubin GPU, NVL144 racks) entered production mid-2026
items.verdict: corrected naming (NVIDIA now says Vera Rubin NVL72, owned by parent/Interconnects); production 'ramping' May 31 2026, shipments 'this fall'

items.fact: AMD MI400 first row from another vendor; Helios vs NVL144 framing
items.verdict: owned by the TPUs and other accelerators sibling

items.fact: SemiAnalysis AgentX: Vera Rubin NVL72 up to 7x tokens per MW vs GB300, 1.4-3x per TCO; 67x not to quote
items.verdict: owned by the parent (s8, verified there: 7x and 1.4-3x; 67x unverifiable); not repeated
